end.summary:
Discussed food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Rohan identified origin labels and compared distances using examples such as apples, spinach, Shimla and Delhi.
Practised links between longer distances, greater fuel use and pollution, plus possible benefits of local food.
Rohan suggested buying vegetables from a local seller and noted that local food may be fresher.
Teach-back was not passed; no misconceptions were recorded.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, finding a food’s origin, and suggesting ways to reduce travel distance. They used the method of checking the origin and connected longer journeys with more fuel and pollution. They also discussed that imported food is not automatically healthier and that local food may be fresher; this mix-up was addressed during the lesson. At home, ask Rohan to compare two foods by checking their origin and explaining which travelled farther and why that matters.
